dedupe_keys.name: mobilitydb moving object trajectory database on postgresql and postgis

description: MobilityDB is an open-source database management system for moving object geospatial trajectories such as GPS traces. It extends PostgreSQL and its spatial extension PostGIS with temporal and spatio-temporal types and operations, so trajectories of vehicles, vessels or people can be stored, queried and analysed in SQL. It is developed by the Computer and Decision Engineering Department of the Université libre de Bruxelles under Esteban Zimányi, is managed by a steering committee, and follows the OGC Moving Features work, in which ULB takes part. A 2025 Springer textbook, Mobility Data Science, explains its use, and a companion repository holds the book's data sets and scripts. Coverage is not geographic: it runs wherever PostgreSQL runs. Access: the code is free on GitHub under the PostgreSQL License, and the documentation under CC BY-SA 3.0. Caveats: it needs a PostgreSQL server and SQL skills. It supports storing and analysing AIS, GPS and transit trajectories for network flow, digital twin and resilience studies. It complements the NGSIM, T-Drive and NYC TLC trip data catalogued here.
